lawyer:
Jagadish Chandra Sarker, Advocate instructed by Nurul Islam Bhuiya, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Petitioners
Chowdhury Md. Zahangir, Advocate-on-Record ------ For Respondents

Amir Hossain @ Abdul Mannan and others ------ Petitioners
Vs.
Abdul Khaleque and others ------- Respondents
full_judgment:
Nazmun Ara Sultana, J. This Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal, at the instance of the defendants, is directed against the judgment and order dated 30.07.2013 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2921 of 2010 making the rule absolute and thereby setting aside the judgment and order dated 02.05.2010 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Comilla in Title Appeal No. 481 of 2007 allowing the present defendant-leave-petitioner's prayer for local investigation to identify the land mentioned in a 'nadabipatra' dated 26.03.1919-the exhibit-'Dha'. The short facts relevant for the purpose of disposal of this civil petition for leave to appeal are that the respondent Nos. 1 to 9 herein, as plaintiffs, filed Title Suit No. 18 of 1999 for getting partition of 2.27 acres of land out of 3.46 acres of land of C.S. Plot No. 531. This plot was recorded in 4 C.S. Khatians being Nos. 152, 153, 156 and 157. In C.S. Khatian Nos. 153 and 156 the plaintiffs claimed their share by inheritance from Abbas Ali. 

 2. The defendant Nos. 26 to 28 and 37-48 filed a written statement raising objection to the claim of the plaintiffs in respect of the land of only 2 khatians being Nos. 153 and 156 on the basis of a 'nadabipatara' dated 26.03.1919 executed by Abbas Ali, the predecessor of the plaintiffs. In this 'nadabipatara' the land has been described with reference to the boundary holders and without any reference to plot number or khatian number. The defendant Nos. 43, 44, 46 and 47 also filed a separate written statement raising claim similar to the said contesting defendants. Some other defendants also appeared in that suit and also prayed for saham. 

 3. After contested hearing, the trial court decreed the suit in part by the judgment and decree dated 31.07.2001. Against that part decree, the plaintiffs preferred Title Appeal No. 180 of 2001 which was heard and disposed of by the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Comilla. This appellate court recorded a finding that the 'nadabipatra' (exhibit-Dha) did not attract the land of C.S. Khatian No. 153 and that the land described in that deed was recorded in C.S. Khatian No. 156 and that Abbas Ali did not relinquish his interest in favour of the defendants by that 'nadabipatra'. However, the appellate court did not ascertain the share of the plaintiffs or the defendants as the said court found that there was defect of party. Accordingly, the appellate court set aside the trial court's judgment and sent the suit on remand with a specific direction to remove the defect of party and for retrial after giving opportunity to the parties to adduce further evidence. Accordingly, before the trial court the defect of party was removed and the trial court, after hearing the parties, delivered the judgment dated 19.08.2007 partly decreeing the suit. 

 4. Against this judgment and decree, the defendants preferred Title Appeal No. 481 of 2007. During pendency of this appeal, the defendant-appellants filed an application under Order 26 Rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for local investigation by relaying the land described in the 'nadabipatra' dated 16.03.1919-the exhibit-'Dha'. The learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Comilla allowed that prayer by the order dated 02.05.2010 against which the plaintiff-respondents preferred the above mentioned Civil Revision No. 2921 of 2010 and obtained rule. A Single Bench of the High Court Division, after hearing both the parties, made that rule absolute and consequently set aside the impugned order dated 02.05.2010 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Comilla in Title Appeal No. 481 of 2007 allowing the prayer for local investigation. The High Court Division, upon hearing the learned Advocates of both the sides and on analysis of the facts and circumstances, found out that in the earlier appeal being Title Appeal No. 180 of 2001 the appellate court made specific findings as to the 'nadabipatra' dated 26.03.1919-the exhibit-Dha and about the identity, of the land of that 'nadahipatra' and also about correctness of C.S. Khatian Nos. 153 and 156 and pointed out also that against these findings and decision of the appellate court passed in Title Appeal No. 180 of 2001 the defendants did not prefer any revision and in the circumstances now, in the second appeal, the same court cannot re-open the question of identity of the land of the 'nadabipatra' by allowing the prayer for local investigation for identifying the land of this 'nadabipatra' the exhibit-'Dha'.
